display_name: The monthly net income, in a month of 2026, of a household with one employed parent: income tax for tax year 2026 and its twelfth, national insurance deducted from the salary, the child allowance and the net, composed from six rows encoding the Income Tax Ordinance and the National Insurance Law

run.method: one agent, one session, no sub-agents, from BRIEF.md

language.note: Identifiers and comments are English (@lang en). The few Hebrew runs are copied from the two deposited sources and cited by line.

composes.provisions: NII s 1 (as needed), ss 334, 337, Schedule J (v0.2.0)

vendoring: The l4 CLI cannot import across directories, so vendor.sh copies the rows' 36 rule, noun and published-figure modules flat into this directory (git-ignored) and VENDORED.sha256 pins each by sha256, row and commons commit; check.sh runs vendor.sh --check first. Each il07-adapter-il0N.l4 imports this row's nouns and one row only. See RECONCILE.md section 1.
scope: Answered: months of 2026, for a household with one employed resident parent paid the same salary every month of 2026, possibly a spouse with no income, and the parent's own children. Composed: the s 121 tax and the s 121B additional tax (IL-03), less the credit points of ss 34, 36, 36A (IL-01) and of s 66(c) where a separate calculation governs the earner's tax (IL-02), at the 2026 credit-point value from s 120B(e)(1) (IL-03) and the Tax Authority's 2025 figure (IL-01); one twelfth of it (fork K1); the employer's deduction under NII s 342(c) (IL-05) of Schedule J column D (IL-04) on the s 348 income (IL-05); the child allowance under NII ss 65-68 (IL-06), with the s 66 additional-tax exclusion joined to IL-03's s 121B (fork K5). Inputs, not encoded: the health insurance contribution (National Health Insurance Law), the registered spouse (ITO s 64B), s 37 entitlement, residence and insurance statuses, a woman's age under NII Schedule A1 Part D, and whether the earner has any credit or deduction no row encodes. Declined by name: every month outside 2026; a spouse with income; a couple assessed under ITO s 65; a parent without a spouse who has children (ITO s 40(b)); an earner with a credit or deduction under ss 35, 45A, 47 and the like; a salary that varies across the year (ITO s 164 and its Regulations); a month in which a child is born or turns 18 (NII s 72); the rows' own refusals. GAPS.md lists every gap in IL-08's work order.

published_figures.source: Israel Tax Authority monthly withholding booklet 2026, PDF p. 8, Internet Archive capture 20260207101513, sha256 282bb886ccae1cc718840127af378fce88ca37ee3b2b9f00ed2cd44467e86285 (il07-published-figures.l4)

expected_red.why: R1 (2): the National Insurance Institute deducts 7% above the reduced collection threshold where Schedule J's column D items, which row IL-04 computes from, sum to 4.67% (IL-04 fork F4); shown on a household's deduction and net. R2 (1): row IL-02's s 66(c)(4) half point under s 36A is 0.5 for a resident foreign-worker woman where row IL-01 declines s 36A under s 48A. NOTES.md section 6, RECONCILE.md section 3.

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this composition or the six rows against the sources. No independent test pass has been run on this row. Every expected value was worked by hand from the sources and the rows' sourced figures, and checked with exact fractions in a calculator that reads no L4, before the assertions were run.

check.vendored: vendor.sh --check: 36 vendored modules match their sources and VENDORED.sha256
check.note: The 3 errors are exactly the 3 expected failures of il07-tests-expected-red.l4; il07-tests.l4 is 113 of 113 satisfied (27 of them #ASSERT REFUSED with BECAUSE).

forks.K1: The year's tax against a month: one twelfth of the year's tax for a salary the same every month (reported as a share, not as tax withheld); declined otherwise, because withholding is ITO s 164 and Regulations not in the sources.
forks.K2: The 2026 credit-point value: IL-03's s 120B(e)(1) from the 1 January 2024 rounded figure, which is the Tax Authority's published 2025 value (2,904, IL-01); twelve times the booklet's monthly 242 agrees.
forks.K3: Credits are set off against the s 121 tax only, never below nil, and the s 121B additional tax is added after; where the credits exceed the s 121 tax and there is additional tax, declined.
forks.K4: The earner's taxable income is the year's salary in every case answered; a spouse with income is declined; a couple with no separate calculation is declined as s 65.
forks.K5: IL-06's 'income chargeable to additional tax' is read for the tax year in which the month falls: TRUE iff IL-03's s 121B tax for that year is above nil.
forks.K6: IL-06 is asked about the first day of the month; a month in which a child is born or turns 18 after that day is declined (NII s 72).
forks.K7: s 36A's half point is counted once, from IL-01, though IL-02 restates it in s 66(c)(4).
forks.K8: The employee's deduction under NII s 342(c) is a percentage of the s 348 income (Schedule K's maximum and minimum applied), not of the wage paid.
forks.K9: IL-04's column D average-wage argument is not read for 2026; the adapter passes a named refusal there.
forks.K10: The tests' health figure applies the Institute's published employee health rates to the salary up to 51,910; the capstone itself takes the figure as an input.
forks.K11: s 37 entitlement is an input (as in IL-02), FALSE in every test.
